measures.short_title: Affordable housing and veterans housing bond

measures.threshold_note: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure.

measures.campaign: Placed by SEIU-UHW after AB 1113 died; clinics oppose and are challenging it in federal court.

measures.short_title: Fast track CEQA review for essential projects
measures.summary: Speeds and narrows environmental review and judicial challenges under CEQA for housing, water, clean energy and other essential projects.
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: Over 13.7 million in supporter funding; no organized opposition committee reported as of March 31, 2026.

measures.short_title: Ban vehicle miles traveled taxes
measures.summary: Bars state and local taxes or fees based on vehicle miles traveled and bars monitoring or limiting mileage without consent.
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: Referred by the Republican led Legislature, bypassing Gov. Hobbs. No campaign finance figures found.

measures.short_title: Ban race based preferences and DEI mandates
measures.summary: Expands the 2010 affirmative action ban to bar public bodies from race or ethnicity preferences and compelled DEI training or offices.
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: Referred by the Republican led Legislature, bypassing Gov. Hobbs. No campaign finance figures found.

measures.short_title: Voter ID for all voters including mail
measures.summary: Requires government ID for every voter including mail voters, limits voting to citizens, bars foreign election contributions; effective 2028.
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: Referred by the Republican led Legislature, bypassing Gov. Hobbs. No campaign finance figures found. Arizona Supreme Court rejected a challenge to remove it from the ballot.

measures.short_title: Cap local grocery taxes at 2 percent
measures.summary: Caps municipal sales taxes on food for home consumption at 2 percent and requires voter approval for new or higher food taxes.
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: Referred by the Republican led Legislature, bypassing Gov. Hobbs. No campaign finance figures found.

measures.short_title: Designate drug cartels as terrorist organizations
measures.summary: Designates drug cartels as terrorist organizations under state law and directs the state Department of Homeland Security to address them.
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: Referred by the Republican led Legislature, bypassing Gov. Hobbs. No campaign finance figures found. Introduced by House Speaker Steve Montenegro.

measures.short_title: Sex based school sports, restrooms, locker rooms
measures.summary: Requires teams designated by biological sex and bars transgender students from restrooms and locker rooms not matching birth sex.
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: Referred by the Republican led Legislature, bypassing Gov. Hobbs. No campaign finance figures found.

measures.short_title: Restrict photo radar traffic enforcement
measures.summary: Bars new photo radar enforcement; existing speed and red light cameras need local voter approval every 10 years to continue.
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: Referred by the Republican led Legislature, bypassing Gov. Hobbs. No campaign finance figures found.

measures.short_title: Require 60 percent spending on instruction
measures.summary: Requires large school districts to spend at least 60 percent of operational budgets on direct instruction or face Classroom Site Fund cuts.
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: Referred by the Republican led Legislature, bypassing Gov. Hobbs. No campaign finance figures found.

measures.short_title: Raise TABOR cap for K-12 school funding
measures.summary: Raises the TABOR revenue cap and keeps about 4.6 billion in surplus revenue for K-12 education.
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: Referred by Legislature (SB26-135). Colorado Democratic Party supports.

measures.short_title: Police must report undocumented violent offenders to DHS
measures.summary: Requires state and local police to notify federal DHS within 72 hours when a person charged with a violent crime or prior felony is not lawfully present.
measures.threshold_note: Colorado constitutional amendments need 55 percent of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: Citizen initiative; Colorado Democratic Party opposes.

measures.short_title: Constitutional right to natural gas
measures.summary: Creates a consumer right to buy natural gas for cooking or heating and lets utilities and distributors sell it.
measures.threshold_note: Colorado constitutional amendments need 55 percent of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: Citizen initiative; Colorado Democratic Party opposes.

measures.short_title: Constitutional right to hunt and fish
measures.summary: Establishes a constitutional right to hunt, fish and take wildlife using traditional methods.
measures.threshold_note: Colorado constitutional amendments need 55 percent of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: Citizen initiative; Democratic Party took no listed position.

measures.short_title: ID number required on mail ballots
measures.summary: Requires mail voters to give a signature plus an ID number such as last four SSN digits, checked against registration records.
measures.threshold_note: Colorado constitutional amendments need 55 percent of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: Citizen initiative; Colorado Democratic Party opposes.

measures.short_title: Plain language ballot questions
measures.summary: Requires ballot questions be written in plain language at no more than an eighth grade reading level.
measures.threshold_note: Colorado constitutional amendments need 55 percent of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: Citizen initiative; Colorado Democratic Party opposes.

measures.short_title: Limits on mid decade congressional redistricting
measures.summary: Requires both the independent commission and state Supreme Court to approve any mid decade congressional map and bars partisan maps.
measures.threshold_note: Colorado constitutional amendments need 55 percent of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: Citizen initiative; Colorado Democratic Party opposes.

measures.short_title: Graduated income tax for schools and health
measures.summary: Replaces the flat income tax with graduated rates from 3.7 to 8.4 percent, removing TABOR's single rate rule, funding K-12, health care, child care.
measures.threshold_note: Colorado constitutional amendments need 55 percent of votes cast on the measure. Combined constitutional and statutory initiative. Conflicts with Prop 136; if both pass, the one with more yes votes prevails.
measures.campaign: Citizen initiative; Colorado Democratic Party supports; Gov. Polis called it a 2.7 billion tax hike and Denver Gazette editorial board opposes.

measures.short_title: Tougher fentanyl penalties
measures.summary: Raises felony penalties for fentanyl distribution and possession and requires court ordered treatment for low level possession.
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: Citizen initiative; Colorado Democratic Party opposes.

measures.short_title: Life without parole for child sex trafficking
measures.summary: Requires life in prison without parole for those convicted of trafficking children for sexual servitude.
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: Citizen initiative; Democratic Party took no listed position.

measures.short_title: School sports teams by biological sex
measures.summary: Requires student athletes to play on school and college teams matching their biological sex.
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: Citizen initiative; Colorado Democratic Party opposes.

measures.short_title: Ban gender transition surgeries for minors
measures.summary: Bans surgeries on minors intended to change sex characteristics and bars public funds or insurance from paying for them.
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: Citizen initiative; Colorado Democratic Party opposes.

measures.short_title: Cap income tax rate at 4.4 percent
measures.summary: Caps individual and corporate income tax rates at 4.4 percent of federal taxable income.
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority. Competes with Amendment 87; if both pass, the one with more yes votes prevails.
measures.campaign: Citizen initiative; Colorado Democratic Party opposes; Gov. Polis predicted it would pass.

measures.short_title: Sporting goods sales tax for conservation
measures.summary: Exempts sporting goods sales tax revenue from TABOR refunds and dedicates it to water, land, forest conservation and wildfire prevention.
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: Citizen initiative; Colorado Democratic Party opposes.

measures.short_title: More Senate time on judicial appointments
measures.summary: Gives the state Senate 60 days instead of 30 to act on judicial appointments made April 1 through December 31 when not in session.
measures.threshold_note: Must win a majority of all ballots cast in the election; blank votes count as no.
measures.campaign: Referred by Legislature; no organized campaigns reported.

measures.short_title: County tax increment bonds for infrastructure
measures.summary: Lets counties issue bonds for sewer, water and drainage in designated districts repaid from property tax revenue growth, outside debt limits.
measures.threshold_note: Must win a majority of all ballots cast in the election; blank votes count as no.
measures.campaign: Referred by Legislature; supporters say it aids housing; no organized campaigns reported.

measures.short_title: Only Legislature may legalize marijuana and drugs
measures.summary: Gives the Legislature sole power to legalize marijuana, narcotics and other psychoactive substances, blocking legalization by citizen initiative.
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: Referred by Republican legislature; Democrats oppose saying it removes voter power.

measures.short_title: English as official state language
measures.summary: Adds a constitutional provision making English the official language of Idaho.
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: Referred by Republican legislature; opponents note state law already designates English.

measures.short_title: Restore abortion access before viability
measures.summary: Creates a statutory right to reproductive decisions including abortion before fetal viability, with emergencies after, and protects contraception and IVF.
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: Citizen initiative led by organizer Melanie Folwell (Idahoans United for Women and Family); 75,478 signatures; opposed by Idaho Chooses Life.

polls.pollster: Boise State University School of Public Service (2026 Idaho Public Policy Survey)
polls.note: Field dates and n not given in news report; approximate shares (strongly or somewhat support); asked before the measure qualified

measures.short_title: Keep judicial elections nonpartisan
measures.summary: Amends the constitution to require that judicial elections remain nonpartisan.
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: Montanans for Nonpartisan Courts, over 3.3 million raised through June 25; Montana Republican Party opposes.

measures.short_title: Protect initiative and referendum rights
measures.summary: Adds initiative and referendum rights to the Declaration of Rights, applies strict scrutiny to limits, and sets rules for ballot language and signature gathering.
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: Montanans Decide, over 2 million raised; opposed by Rep. Braxton Mitchell side.

measures.short_title: Bar corporate political spending via charter limits
measures.summary: Limits powers of artificial persons so corporations and other entities cannot spend on candidates, ballot measures or parties.
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: Transparent Election Initiative PAC, 305,000 raised, endorsed by former Gov. Steve Bullock; opposed by Montanans for Free Speech.

measures.short_title: Constitutional right to abortion until viability
measures.summary: Second vote to add a right to abortion until fetal viability, or after to protect patient life or health, to the Nevada Constitution.
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority; this is the required second approval of an initiated constitutional amendment first passed in 2024. If it fails, the amendment does not take effect. Passed with 64 percent in 2024.
measures.campaign: Nevadans for Reproductive Freedom support; Nevadans Right to Life oppose. No money figures found.

measures.short_title: Photo voter ID requirement
measures.summary: Second vote to require photo ID to vote in person and an ID number on mail ballots, effective for 2028 elections.
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority; this is the required second approval of an initiated constitutional amendment first passed in 2024. If it fails, the amendment does not take effect. Passed with 73 percent in 2024.
measures.campaign: Backed by Dave Gibbs with support from Gov. Joe Lombardo; critics say unnecessary. No money figures found.

measures.short_title: End pocket veto, require veto explanations
measures.summary: Bills the governor neither signs nor vetoes become law, and the governor must explain any full or partial veto.
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: Co-sponsored by Rep. Matthew McQueen (D); critics call it superfluous.

measures.short_title: Allow school elections with partisan elections
measures.summary: Removes the requirement that school elections be held separately from partisan elections, allowing them on November even year ballots.
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority assumed. It amends Art. VII Sec. 1 (elective franchise), which Art. XIX Sec. 1 has historically shielded with a 3/4 statewide and 2/3 per county requirement; whether that applies was not confirmed.
measures.campaign: Co-sponsored by Sen. Linda Trujillo (D); critics warn of voter fatigue.

measures.short_title: Nominating committee for university regents
measures.summary: Creates nominating committees to recommend university regents to the governor and bars recent party switchers from serving.
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: Co-sponsored by Sen. Jeff Steinborn (D).

measures.short_title: Tie legislator pay to median income
measures.summary: Gives legislators a salary tied to state median household income, with delayed implementation.
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: Referred by Legislature; no campaign details found.

measures.short_title: Senior citizen facilities bond
measures.summary: Authorizes 21,582,213 dollars in general obligation bonds for senior citizen facility improvements and equipment.
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: 2026 Capital Projects GO Bond Act; repaid by property tax levy.

measures.short_title: Library acquisitions bond
measures.summary: Authorizes 19,324,188 dollars in general obligation bonds for academic, public school, public and tribal library resources.
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: 2026 Capital Projects GO Bond Act; repaid by property tax levy.

measures.short_title: Higher education and tribal schools bond
measures.summary: Authorizes 352,225,379 dollars in general obligation bonds for higher education institutions, special schools and tribal schools.
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: 2026 Capital Projects GO Bond Act; repaid by property tax levy.

measures.short_title: Flexible publication of proposed amendments
measures.summary: Replaces the two month newspaper publication rule for proposed amendments, letting lawmakers set the format if notice is given 60 days before the election.
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: Passed Legislature unanimously; no opposition campaign.

measures.short_title: 60 percent vote for tax raising initiatives
measures.summary: Requires 60 percent voter approval for citizen initiatives that create, raise or expand taxes.
measures.threshold_note: Amendment B itself needs a simple majority.
measures.campaign: Sponsored by Sen. Lincoln Fillmore and Rep. Jason Kyle, backed by Utah Taxpayers Association and Taxpayer Shield PAC; opposed by Utahns Protecting Our Constitution (Better Boundaries), described as a million dollar campaign.

measures.short_title: Girls' sports limited to biological females
measures.summary: Bars students defined as biologically male from girls' interschool sports and requires a provider statement verifying sex to participate.
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: Let's Go Washington (Brian Heywood) initiative to the Legislature, 400,000 plus signatures; Legislature did not act; WEA and Northwest Progressive Institute oppose.

measures.short_title: Parents' Bill of Rights reinstatement
measures.summary: Fully reinstates the Parents' Bill of Rights giving parents access to student academic, medical and counseling records and notifications, repealing 2025 changes.
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: Let's Go Washington initiative to the Legislature; Legislature did not act; WEA and LGBTQ advocates oppose.

measures.short_title: Repeal millionaires income tax, ban income taxes
measures.summary: Repeals the 2026 9.9 percent tax on individual income over 1 million and bars state and local income taxes.
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: Let's Go Washington initiative to the people; No campaign backed by Rick Steves and Ken Jennings; court upheld ballot language including fiscal impact statement (about 11.4 billion revenue loss FY2027 to 2031).

measures.short_title: 50 percent homestead property tax exemption
measures.summary: Exempts 50 percent of the assessed value of a qualifying owner occupied primary residence from property tax.
measures.threshold_note: Must receive a majority of all ballots cast in the general election, not just votes on the question; blank votes effectively count as no.
measures.campaign: Sponsored by BCR Initiatives (Brent Bien, Cheryl Aguiar, Rich Weber); first Wyoming initiative on the ballot since 1996; state revenue loss about 92.6 million in FY2028; a group organized against it.

measures.short_title: Repeal open primaries and ranked choice voting
measures.summary: Repeals the top four open primary and ranked choice general elections, restoring party primaries, and repeals 2020 campaign finance disclosure rules.
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: Repeal Now (yes) raised 1.1 million, 846,000 from Aurora Action Network; No on 2 / Protect Alaska's Elections raised 5.75 million, 4 million from Unite America. 2024 repeal failed by 737 votes.

measures.short_title: Only U.S. citizens may vote
measures.summary: Amends state law to provide that only U.S. citizens may vote in any Alaska election.
measures.threshold_note: Simple majority of votes cast on the measure.
measures.campaign: Citizen initiative (indirect statute); no campaign finance found.

gaps: Oregon: no statewide measures on Nov 3 per Oregon SOS (Measure 120 gas tax referendum was on May 19, 2026 and failed). Alaska Ballot Measure 1 (campaign contribution limits) was on the Aug 18 primary ballot, so excluded. Washington: official ballot designations unconfirmed; sources use IL26-638/I-638, IL26-001/I-001, IP26-645/I-645; SOS page could not be fetched. No WA SJRs found. Arizona: one source called the school spending measure Prop 143; azfamily, Axios and Arizona Mirror say Prop 320, used here. Montana: SOS lists only CI-132, CI-133, I-194 as qualified; no 2025 legislative referrals found but not independently confirmed. Utah: only Amendments A and B per Deseret News; HB 267 union referendum not on ballot (not separately confirmed why). Wyoming: SOS 2026 propositions PDF shows only the initiative; SJ7 abortion amendment failed introduction. Idaho: initiative ballot label (Proposition number) not found; Boise State poll lacks field dates and n. Polls not found for any AZ, CO, NV, AK, MT, NM, HI, WY measure or ID HJR 4/HJR 6 within budget. KSNV aired voter ID polling graphic for NV with no published numbers. PPIC July 2026 reportedly had Prop 45 at 73 percent yes and PPIC February had Prop 1 at 49 percent yes but full numbers/dates were not retrieved so excluded. PPIC Sept 2026 undecided shares not reported. Let's Go Washington I-638 poll is sponsor internal with undisclosed pollster and only month level dates. NM Amendment 2 possible supermajority requirement unverified. Search budget of 40 exhausted; Ballotpedia main state pages were stale or robots blocked.
